title: Find All People With Secret
statement:
There are `n` people labelled `0` to `n - 1`. Each entry `meetings[i] = [x_i, y_i, time_i]` records that persons `x_i` and `y_i` meet at time `time_i`; one person can be in several meetings held at the same time.

Person `0` starts with a secret and tells it to person `firstPerson` at time `0`. From then on, whenever a meeting takes place and either attendee already knows the secret at that moment, the other attendee learns it as well. Passing the secret on takes no time: someone who learns it at time `t` can pass it along in any other meeting held at that same time `t`.

Return every person who knows the secret once all the meetings are over, in any order.
signature: List<Integer> findAllPeople(int n, int[][] meetings, int firstPerson)
notes:
## Intuition

Meetings only matter in time order, and all meetings that share a time behave like one graph: the secret floods through any connected group that contains someone who already knows it. Simulating each time with repeated passes works but is slow. Union-find handles each time in near-constant work per meeting: link everyone who meets at that time, then ask who ended up in the same set as person `0`.

## Approach

1. Start every person in their own set, then join `0` with `firstPerson`. `union` always keeps the smaller root, so `0` stays the root of the knowers' set.
2. Sort `meetings` by time.
3. For each block of meetings from `start` to `end` with the same `time`, union the two attendees of every meeting.
4. Walk the block again: any attendee whose root is not `0` did not learn the secret, so reset `parent[x] = x`. Otherwise a later meeting could wrongly leak the secret into this temporary group.
5. Collect every `person` whose root is `0`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 6`, `firstPerson = 1`. First `union(0, 1)` puts `{0, 1}` together. At time 5, `union(1, 2)` gives `{0, 1, 2}`; both roots are `0`, so nothing is reset. At time 8, `union(2, 3)` adds 3. At time 10, `union(1, 5)` adds 5. Person 4 never meets anyone, so the result is `[0, 1, 2, 3, 5]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m log m + (m + n) log n): sorting the meetings costs O(m log m), and with path halving each `find` is amortized O(log n) (nearly constant in practice).
- Space: O(n) for `parent` (plus the sort).

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the reset: if 2 and 3 meet at time 1 and 1 tells 2 at time 2, person 3 must not learn the secret.
- Processing meetings of the same time one by one in input order misses chains like `[3,4,t]` listed before `[1,3,t]`.
- Resetting must only touch people from the current time block; everyone else is either already a knower or alone.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `parent` | union-find parent of each person |
| `find`, `union` | root lookup with path halving, and merge keeping the smaller root |
| `start`, `end` | the block of meetings sharing one `time` |
| `x`, `y` | the two attendees of a meeting |
| `result` | people whose root is `0` |
